transcriptText:
Two cards to come, with a flush draw. So you multiply by four... right? Here's the catch. Same flop, two bets. Up top, they go all-in. Below, they bet half the pot. Which rule fits each? Make your picks.

Only a diamond wins here. Nine are still unseen, so that's 9 outs. All-in, nobody can bet again. You see the turn and the river for one price. 9 × 4... about 36%. A normal bet only buys the turn. Miss, and they can bet again. So it's 9 × 2... about 18%.

Are these shortcuts any good? One card, exactly: 9 in 47... about 19%. Both cards? Deal every turn and river pair, all 1,081 of them. 378 bring a diamond. 35%. Close enough to decide with.

Your turn. Ten-nine of hearts, on eight, seven, two... and they shove all-in. Pick the rule first. 8 outs, and you see both cards. × 4... 32%. Exactly? 31.5%. Big draws run high, though. 15 outs × 4 says 60... it's really about 54%. So, × 2 for one card. × 4 only when you see both for this price. Up next: equity.
